claims.text: The trip record shows the trip was terminated by the RIDER, not the driver: cancellation_reason_code is RIDER_CANCELLED and cancelled_by is RIDER. POL-NS-01 limb (d) requires the trip to be terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. None of those three codes appears anywhere in this record, so limb (d) fails and the no-show fee is not chargeable under the anchor clause.

The driver's own trace shows a single continuous in-geofence run of 382 seconds, from 15:14:06 to 15:20:28, and the rider cancelled at 15:20:31. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec). The dwell therefore exceeded the free waiting period by 202 seconds, so the shortfall route in POL-NS-06 does not rescue the fee either — the fee cannot be refunded on a waiting-period-shortfall theory. I concede this point: the dwell was long enough.

The rider's cancellation came 6 minutes 7 seconds after the driver was matched (accepted_at 15:09:24, cancelled_at 15:20:31), well outside the 180 second grace_after_match_sec in platform_policy. So POL-NS-10 limb (a) does not make the cancellation non-chargeable, and limb (f) is the operative provision: a rider's own cancellation after the grace is chargeable at platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd whether or not the driver had arrived. I concede this point against my side.

POL-NS-10 limb (f) refunds the fee in full where the record shows the driver had not begun moving toward the pickup within the grace. Here the driver began navigating 8 seconds after assignment (driver_en_route at 15:09:32), so that exception does not apply. I concede this point too.

The rider's own chat message at 15:18:16 — 'sorry cant make it, cancelling' — is an admission that the rider could not make the pickup and was cancelling. That is the rider's own statement of the reason for the cancellation, and it is inconsistent with the claim now advanced that 'no no-show fee should apply' because the driver did not cancel. The rider's claim text mischaracterises the record: the rider did cancel, and the fee follows from the rider's own cancellation under POL-NS-10(f).

The rider's GPS track places the rider's device at a mean distance of 767.9 m from the pickup pin throughout the waiting window, with a minimum of 764.6 m — far outside the 100 m rider_presence_radius_m for a STANDARD zone. The rider was not at or near the pickup point when the driver was waiting there. This defeats any suggestion that the rider was present and trying to coordinate, and it supports the driver's account that he waited at the pin.

The driver's trace shows 39 qualifying in-geofence fixes within the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, a continuous run of 382 seconds, and the driver's own chat message 'im at the pickup' at 15:14:36. The driver arrived and held position. The rider's claim that 'the driver did not cancel' is true but irrelevant: the fee is chargeable on the rider's own post-grace cancellation under POL-NS-10(f), not on a driver-initiated no-show under POL-NS-01.

The fare breakdown shows the cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 was charged and payment_status is CHARGED, with refund_issued_sgd 0.0. The fee reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of 4.50, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect. The present state stands: the rider's claim is not supported and the charge remains.

The driver's profile shows no_show_terminations_30d of 2 and completed_trips_30d of 101. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check requires BOTH no_show_terminations_30d of 4 or more AND a ratio above 0.08. Here the count is 2, below the threshold, so the anti-farming branch does not trip and the driver's compensation is not withheld on that ground. I note this because it is the only profile field POL-NS-07 permits me to cite, and it does not assist the rider.

The rider's profile shows no_show_disputes_30d of 0 and disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0 on both sides. Neither POL-NS-09(c) nor POL-NS-09(d) is engaged: there is no pattern of repeat no-show disputes between this rider and this driver, and no abuse indicator on the rider's side. Escalation on those grounds is not available.

The traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-02739-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0. Under POL-NS-06 limb (i), a MISSING traffic_advisory makes the accumulated-dwell limb unavailable, and asserting it against a MISSING artifact triggers POL-NS-09 rather than exonerating anyone. I do not rely on it, and I note that its absence cannot be used to reduce the required minimum dwell or to excuse any shortfall.

The rider's claim text asserts that 'the driver did not cancel, so no no-show fee should apply.' That is a non sequitur. The fee here is not a driver-initiated no-show fee under POL-NS-01; it is a rider-cancellation fee under POL-NS-10(f), which is chargeable on the rider's own cancellation after the grace period whether or not the driver had arrived. The rider's stated ground for the refund does not engage the clause that actually governs this cancellation.

claims.text: The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event for this trip at 2026-08-29T15:14:06+08:00, satisfying POL-NS-01 limb (a). The same record shows the free waiting period of 180 seconds started two seconds later at 15:14:08, and the rider cancelled at 15:20:31 — 383 seconds after the wait timer began, well past the 180 second free waiting period in force for this trip under trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec.

The driver's own GPS trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for a continuous qualifying run of 382 seconds, from 15:14:06 to 15:20:28, with 39 qualifying fixes. That is more than double the 180 second minimum dwell for this zone class, so POL-NS-01 limb (c) is satisfied on the driver's own evidence, not merely on the platform's arrival tap.

The arrival marker is not false. The trace shows the driver stationary at the pin from the moment of the 'I'm Here' tap — the longest qualifying in-geofence run begins at 15:14:06, the exact timestamp of the arrival event, and the driver's minimum recorded distance from the pin is 0.11 m. There is no expressway-speed fix at the arrival timestamp, so POL-NS-05 does not displace the waiting clock and the recomputed clock is the same as the recorded one.

The rider's own cancellation is chargeable under POL-NS-10(f): she cancelled herself, in the chat log, after the grace period, and none of the four exceptions applies — the driver began moving toward the pickup within the grace (driver_en_route at 15:09:32, eight seconds after assignment), he arrived at 15:14:06, he never asked her to cancel, and the vehicle and driver matched the booking. Her own message reads 'sorry cant make it, cancelling'.

Independently of the no-show route, POL-NS-10(g) applies: the rider cancelled after the driver had arrived under POL-NS-02 and the in-geofence dwell under POL-NS-01(c) had already exceeded free_wait_sec (382 seconds against 180). The fee therefore stands at platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of SGD 4.50 as if the trip had been terminated for a no-show, and POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout.

The fare ledger reconciles: the cancellation fee line is SGD 4.50, which equals the net figure produced by the resolution rule from trip_record.platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, and the payment status is CHARGED with no refund issued. There is no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect, so the fee is chargeable in the amount shown and the driver's compensation is computed on that net figure.

The driver is entitled to compensation at 80 percent of the net cancellation fee in force, which the ledger computes as SGD 3.60 of SGD 4.50, and the anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the threshold of 4, and 2 divided by completed_trips_30d of 101 is 0.0198, below the 0.08 rate. Both limbs of the POL-NS-07 check must hold and neither does, so compensation is paid rather than withheld.

The rider's exoneration route under POL-NS-04 fails on its own terms. Her only message during the waiting window was sent at 15:18:16, after the driver had already posted 'im at the pickup' at 15:14:36, and it is a cancellation notice rather than a locating or coordinating message; and the trace shows her device stationary at a mean distance of roughly 768 m from the pin, outside the 100 m STANDARD rider presence radius, with zero qualifying rider fixes. Limb (a) and limb (c) both fail, so the clause does not apply.

The rider's claim that 'no no-show fee should apply' because she cancelled herself is not supported by the policy: POL-NS-10(f) makes a rider's own post-grace cancellation chargeable whether or not the driver had arrived, and POL-NS-10(g) makes it chargeable as a no-show where the driver had arrived and served the dwell. The present state — CHARGED, no refund issued — should stand, and the driver should be paid.

The missing traffic advisory does not help the rider and does not hurt the driver here. EV-ADVIS-02739-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0, so POL-NS-06 limb (i) is unavailable and no accumulated dwell across separate intervals can be claimed — but the driver does not need it, because his dwell is a single continuous 382 second run inside the geofence, already above the 180 second minimum. The absence is citable but it is not load-bearing for this fee.

ruling.explanation: To both parties: this is about the SGD 4.50 charged when the rider cancelled trip TRP-02739. The rider is right on the facts and wrong on the outcome. She did cancel the trip herself — the trip record shows cancelled_by RIDER and cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED — so this was never a driver-terminated no-show, and the anchor clause POL-NS-01 does require the driver to have ended the trip under RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. None of those codes appears, so limb (d) fails and the fee cannot stand on POL-NS-01. That point is accepted. But it does not make the fee refundable. POL-NS-10 governs the rider's own cancellation: it came 6 minutes 7 seconds after the driver was matched (accepted_at 15:09:24, cancelled_at 15:20:31), far outside the 180-second grace_after_match_sec in platform_policy, so limb (a) does not excuse it. None of limb (f)'s four exceptions applies — the driver began moving 8 seconds after assignment, arrived and waited, never asked her to cancel, and the vehicle matched the booking. Her own message 'sorry cant make it, cancelling' at 15:18:16 confirms the reason. POL-NS-10(g) then applies: the driver had arrived under POL-NS-02 (39 qualifying in-geofence fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD radius, a continuous 382-second dwell at the pin, minimum recorded distance 0.11 m), and that dwell had already exceeded the 180-second free waiting period when she cancelled. The arrival marker is not false — the 'I'm Here' tap at 15:14:06 coincides with the first qualifying in-geofence fix — so POL-NS-05 does not displace the clock. The SVG 4.50 fee therefore stands, and the fare ledger reconciles to it (no POL-NS-08(d) defect). The rider's exoneration route under POL-NS-04 fails on its own terms: her only waiting-window message was the cancellation notice, not a locating or coordinating message (limb (a)), and her device sat roughly 768 m from the pin (limb (c)). Because the fee stands, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the net fee — SGD 3.60 of SGD 4.50, the figure the ledger computes. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the required 4, and 2/101 = 0.02, below the 0.08 rate, so compensation is paid rather than withheld. On the driver's profile and the rider's, no escalation ground is engaged: POL-NS-09(c) needs 2 or more same-pair disputes (both sides show 0), POL-NS-09(d) needs 3 or more rider no-show disputes or a tripped anti-farming check (rider shows 0, check does not trip). No clause produces a referral here, so the referrals list is empty, and no clause produces a driver-education item. Confidence is not capped below 1.0: every artifact carrying a deciding fact — the trip record, the GPS trace, the chat log and the fare breakdown — is at weight 1.0, and the missing traffic advisory (weight 0.0) carries no fact this ruling rests on; two claims that cited it without naming its MISSING_ARTIFACT code were discarded by the referee. The monetary effect, SGD 3.60, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold in POL-GEN-05, so it executes automatically on issue. In short: the rider's charge stands as it presently is, and the driver is paid SGD 3.60.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your claim is that you cancelled and the driver did not, so no no-show fee can apply. You are right on the narrow point, and it does not refund you. The driver-terminated no-show route in POL-NS-01 fails on limb (d): EV-TRIP-02739 records cancelled_by RIDER and cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED, and none of RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT appears. ledger.claim: The trip record shows the trip was terminated by the RIDER, not the driver: cancellation_reason_code is RIDER_CANCELLED and cancelled_by is RIDER. POL-NS-01 limb (d) requires the trip to be terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. None of those three codes appears anywhere in this record, so limb (d) fails and the no-show fee is not chargeable under the anchor clause.

The driver's own trace shows a single continuous in-geofence run of 382 seconds, from 15:14:06 to 15:20:28, and the rider cancelled at 15:20:31. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec). The dwell therefore exceeded the free waiting period by 202 seconds, so the shortfall route in POL-NS-06 does not rescue the fee either — the fee cannot be refunded on a waiting-period-shortfall theory. I concede this point: the dwell was long enough.

The rider's cancellation came 6 minutes 7 seconds after the driver was matched (accepted_at 15:09:24, cancelled_at 15:20:31), well outside the 180 second grace_after_match_sec in platform_policy. So POL-NS-10 limb (a) does not make the cancellation non-chargeable, and limb (f) is the operative provision: a rider's own cancellation after the grace is chargeable at platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd whether or not the driver had arrived. I concede this point against my side.

POL-NS-10 limb (f) refunds the fee in full where the record shows the driver had not begun moving toward the pickup within the grace. Here the driver began navigating 8 seconds after assignment (driver_en_route at 15:09:32), so that exception does not apply. I concede this point too.

The rider's own chat message at 15:18:16 — 'sorry cant make it, cancelling' — is an admission that the rider could not make the pickup and was cancelling. That is the rider's own statement of the reason for the cancellation, and it is inconsistent with the claim now advanced that 'no no-show fee should apply' because the driver did not cancel. The rider's claim text mischaracterises the record: the rider did cancel, and the fee follows from the rider's own cancellation under POL-NS-10(f).

The rider's GPS track places the rider's device at a mean distance of 767.9 m from the pickup pin throughout the waiting window, with a minimum of 764.6 m — far outside the 100 m rider_presence_radius_m for a STANDARD zone. The rider was not at or near the pickup point when the driver was waiting there. This defeats any suggestion that the rider was present and trying to coordinate, and it supports the driver's account that he waited at the pin.

The driver's trace shows 39 qualifying in-geofence fixes within the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, a continuous run of 382 seconds, and the driver's own chat message 'im at the pickup' at 15:14:36. The driver arrived and held position. The rider's claim that 'the driver did not cancel' is true but irrelevant: the fee is chargeable on the rider's own post-grace cancellation under POL-NS-10(f), not on a driver-initiated no-show under POL-NS-01.

The fare breakdown shows the cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 was charged and payment_status is CHARGED, with refund_issued_sgd 0.0. The fee reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of 4.50, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect. The present state stands: the rider's claim is not supported and the charge remains.

The driver's profile shows no_show_terminations_30d of 2 and completed_trips_30d of 101. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check requires BOTH no_show_terminations_30d of 4 or more AND a ratio above 0.08. Here the count is 2, below the threshold, so the anti-farming branch does not trip and the driver's compensation is not withheld on that ground. I note this because it is the only profile field POL-NS-07 permits me to cite, and it does not assist the rider.

The rider's profile shows no_show_disputes_30d of 0 and disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0 on both sides. Neither POL-NS-09(c) nor POL-NS-09(d) is engaged: there is no pattern of repeat no-show disputes between this rider and this driver, and no abuse indicator on the rider's side. Escalation on those grounds is not available.

ledger.claim: The rider's claim text asserts that 'the driver did not cancel, so no no-show fee should apply.' That is a non sequitur. The fee here is not a driver-initiated no-show fee under POL-NS-01; it is a rider-cancellation fee under POL-NS-10(f), which is chargeable on the rider's own cancellation after the grace period whether or not the driver had arrived. The rider's stated ground for the refund does not engage the clause that actually governs this cancellation.

The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event for this trip at 2026-08-29T15:14:06+08:00, satisfying POL-NS-01 limb (a). The same record shows the free waiting period of 180 seconds started two seconds later at 15:14:08, and the rider cancelled at 15:20:31 — 383 seconds after the wait timer began, well past the 180 second free waiting period in force for this trip under trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec.

The driver's own GPS trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for a continuous qualifying run of 382 seconds, from 15:14:06 to 15:20:28, with 39 qualifying fixes. That is more than double the 180 second minimum dwell for this zone class, so POL-NS-01 limb (c) is satisfied on the driver's own evidence, not merely on the platform's arrival tap.

The arrival marker is not false. The trace shows the driver stationary at the pin from the moment of the 'I'm Here' tap — the longest qualifying in-geofence run begins at 15:14:06, the exact timestamp of the arrival event, and the driver's minimum recorded distance from the pin is 0.11 m. There is no expressway-speed fix at the arrival timestamp, so POL-NS-05 does not displace the waiting clock and the recomputed clock is the same as the recorded one.

The rider's own cancellation is chargeable under POL-NS-10(f): she cancelled herself, in the chat log, after the grace period, and none of the four exceptions applies — the driver began moving toward the pickup within the grace (driver_en_route at 15:09:32, eight seconds after assignment), he arrived at 15:14:06, he never asked her to cancel, and the vehicle and driver matched the booking. Her own message reads 'sorry cant make it, cancelling'.

Independently of the no-show route, POL-NS-10(g) applies: the rider cancelled after the driver had arrived under POL-NS-02 and the in-geofence dwell under POL-NS-01(c) had already exceeded free_wait_sec (382 seconds against 180). The fee therefore stands at platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of SGD 4.50 as if the trip had been terminated for a no-show, and POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout.

The fare ledger reconciles: the cancellation fee line is SGD 4.50, which equals the net figure produced by the resolution rule from trip_record.platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, and the payment status is CHARGED with no refund issued. There is no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect, so the fee is chargeable in the amount shown and the driver's compensation is computed on that net figure.

The driver is entitled to compensation at 80 percent of the net cancellation fee in force, which the ledger computes as SGD 3.60 of SGD 4.50, and the anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the threshold of 4, and 2 divided by completed_trips_30d of 101 is 0.0198, below the 0.08 rate. Both limbs of the POL-NS-07 check must hold and neither does, so compensation is paid rather than withheld.

The rider's exoneration route under POL-NS-04 fails on its own terms. Her only message during the waiting window was sent at 15:18:16, after the driver had already posted 'im at the pickup' at 15:14:36, and it is a cancellation notice rather than a locating or coordinating message; and the trace shows her device stationary at a mean distance of roughly 768 m from the pin, outside the 100 m STANDARD rider presence radius, with zero qualifying rider fixes. Limb (a) and limb (c) both fail, so the clause does not apply.

The rider's claim that 'no no-show fee should apply' because she cancelled herself is not supported by the policy: POL-NS-10(f) makes a rider's own post-grace cancellation chargeable whether or not the driver had arrived, and POL-NS-10(g) makes it chargeable as a no-show where the driver had arrived and served the dwell. The present state — CHARGED, no refund issued — should stand, and the driver should be paid.

The missing traffic advisory does not help the rider and does not hurt the driver here. EV-ADVIS-02739-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0, so POL-NS-06 limb (i) is unavailable and no accumulated dwell across separate intervals can be claimed — but the driver does not need it, because his dwell is a single continuous 382 second run inside the geofence, already above the 180 second minimum. The absence is citable but it is not load-bearing for this fee.
